A1.justification: Despite retitling, both PDFs describe the same summary-centroid clustering work, retaining k-LLMmeans, its streaming extension, datasets, and many results. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original static and streaming clustering experiments, centroid-distance measurements, and a StackExchange case study, including extended results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original clustering results and adds k-NLPmeans evaluations and BANK77 prompt and summary-length sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: v3 introduces k-NLPmeans: cluster sentences are summarized using centroid ranking, TextRank, or LSA, then re-embedded as centroids (Section 3.1). These alternatives also enter the mini-batch framework, making LLM summarization optional. The existing k-LLMmeans procedure and weighted mini-batch update are substantially retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BANK77, CLINC, GoEmo, MASSIVE domain and intent clustering, the same 2020–2023 StackExchange streams, and the 2021 AI-site case study. Appendix A retains the dataset descriptions and filtering. New summarizer and sensitivity experiments use existing coverage.

E2.justification: For retained CLINC, GoEmo, and MASSIVE(D) experiments with DistilBERT, e5-large, and S-BERT, v3 omits the k-medoids, GMM, agglomerative, and spectral comparisons supplied by v2 Appendix Tables 6–8. These comparisons now retain k-means and add k-NLPmeans. The main classical, streaming, and external LLM comparator sets otherwise remain, including ClusterLLM, IDAS, and LLMEdgeRefine.

E3.justification: New experiments specify q=5 for extractive summaries and BANK77 evaluations varying prompt wording and q over 3, 5, 10, and 15 (Table 9). Shared experiments retain the 120-update budget, summarization schedules, embedding models, metrics, and chronological streaming batches.

E4.justification: v3 adds comparisons of three extractive summarizers with single versus multiple updates and dedicated prompt/summary-length sensitivity analyses (Appendix B.2). It also removes much of v2's cross-embedding comparison of four LLM variants and the reported single-step streaming ablations. Qualitative evidence is reduced by removing the banking-centroid illustration and the AI Mathematics case-study trajectory.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix B.1 specifies ten seeds for static simulations; v3 Section 5 states five seeds per method setting while retaining ten-seed baseline wording. Both already report standard deviations and five-seed streaming evaluations. The changed run-count reporting does not establish that retained results were recomputed.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive k-NLPmeans scores, sensitivity outcomes, and per-run cost/timing reports, while omitting many detailed appendix results and the single/FS-single streaming rows. Most shared k-LLMmeans scores remain unchanged. Table 1 revises MASSIVE(I) ACC from 56.4 to 56.7 for FS-multiple and from 56.7 to 56.6 for spectral clustering; these are reported numerical revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a formal sentence multiset and q-sentence summarization operator defining the new centroid update (Equation 3). The existing objective and LLM centroid formula remain. v3 also replaces v2's O(kl) LLM-call statement with k calls per summarization step. Neither version supplies a convergence proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution broadens from LLM-generated centroids to an LLM-optional summary-centroid framework, explicitly claiming deterministic, offline operation through k-NLPmeans. The abstract, introduction, and discussion adopt this broader scope. Objective preservation is qualified as applying between summary steps, narrowing v2's broader provable-descent framing.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations attributing LLM advantages to summary quality and extractive streaming weaknesses to noisy, heterogeneous posts. It discusses non-text extensions and argues that pretraining exposure gives no unfair advantage. Section 7 adds causal interpretations involving technology releases and policy developments to retained trajectories. v2's separate broader-impact discussion and specific human-validation guidance disappear.

D1.justification: v3 adds sentence-similarity and summary-length details, exact sensitivity-test prompts, and a code-reproduction URL with a README pointer. v2 Appendix C's aggregate week-long runtime, approximately $700 expense, and 120-million-token account are removed; Section 9 instead provides per-run laptop costs and timings. These describe different resource quantities, not demonstrated efficiency gains.

R1.justification: v3 positions novelty around periodically integrating established summarizers into k-means, adding TextRank, centroid-summarization, and LSA references and broader summarization context. Related work adds BERTopic and distinguishes DeepCluster's encoder training from the proposed fixed-embedding setting. Model documentation and literature supporting the expanded case-study interpretations are also added.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, advantages, results narrative, case-study interpretation, and discussion. Section 3 separates classical and LLM summarizers, the contribution statement is reorganized, and the appendices are restructured. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond documenting new experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with connecting arrows and revised labels. v2 Figure 2 is removed, and Figure 3 becomes v3 Figure 2 with one trajectory removed. Tables gain k-NLPmeans rows; appendix dataset-specific grids are replaced by reorganized main-result tables with standard deviations and a new sensitivity table. Both algorithms move into Appendix C.

improvement.justification: The LLM-free comparisons and prompt/summary-length tests better establish what summary-derived centroids contribute, while more careful objective-preservation language and an explicit reproduction link improve clarity. These gains are tempered by reduced appendix comparison coverage and new reporting inconsistencies, including k-NLPmeans CLINC ACC of 80.0 in Table 2 versus 80.2 in Table 6. The net improvement is therefore limited.
